text: I’ll model the fluid directly in metres as the 12 mm annular gap, subtracting 36 constant-8 mm tangential-width radial vanes. The resulting 36 disconnected passage volumes will be meshed conformally with swept prismatic elements; their common patch groups will be the two axial friction-face surfaces, vane walls, inner inlet, and outer outlet. First I’m building and inspecting the coarse CAD fluid volume.

The image confirms the intended annular gap and radial vane pattern. The CAD kernel reports one compound solid because adjacent passages meet at exact circular/vane corner tolerances, so I will not use that boolean topology for meshing. Instead I’ll construct each mathematically bounded passage independently. Before volume meshing, I’m exporting the five requested patch groups as consistently tessellated metre-scale STL surfaces.

The exact passage opening is 5.174° at the 190 mm bore and 7.135° at the 320 mm rim; this variation is the geometric consequence of a constant 8 mm vane width. I’ll now generate a coarse swept mesh with 13 radial, 4 circumferential, and 3 gapwise cells per passage (5,616 hexahedra nominally), preserving the five physical patch names.

The coarse mesh contains exactly 5,616 hexahedra and all five requested physical surface groups. I’ll convert it to OpenFOAM and run the binding mesh check now; this also verifies whether all disconnected passage regions and boundary faces survived conversion correctly.

Conversion stopped before touching the mesh because an empty OpenFOAM case lacks `system/controlDict`. I’ll add only the minimal case metadata required by OpenFOAM utilities, then repeat conversion and checking.

Mesh conversion succeeded. This OpenFOAM release also requires empty `fvSchemes` and `fvSolution` dictionaries even for `checkMesh`; I’ll add those mesh-utility prerequisites and rerun the full topology/geometry check.
The checker reads mandatory scheme subdictionaries even though it does not solve. I’ll supply inert defaults (no fields or boundary conditions) and rerun.

`checkMesh` now passes all topology and geometry tests. It identifies the expected 36 disconnected flow regions, each with 156 hexahedra. I’ll make a final visual inspection of the converted OpenFOAM mesh and verify patch face totals and metre-scale bounds from the written mesh.

The converted mesh image shows all 36 open radial passages with the intended swept topology. One correction to the CAD bookkeeping is needed: the initial compound subtraction did not subtract all touching vane tools reliably, as its volume disagrees with the meshed passage volume. I’ll rebuild that CAD boolean sequentially and also instantiate the two given 10 mm friction plates (outside the fluid mesh) so their thickness and 12 mm separation are explicitly measured.

The explicit plate dimensions are correct. The remaining CAD volume mismatch traces to composing rotations onto an already located vane; I’ll correct the transform order by rotating a freshly translated vane about the global disc axis, then remeasure against the exact passage construction used by Gmsh.

The corrected list contains 36 vane objects, but the boolean still removes only 18 unique placements, indicating a transform-composition issue rather than a meshing issue. I’ll inspect representative vane centroids and switch to explicit trigonometric locations if they overlap.

The representative centroids confirm all 36 CAD vanes are uniquely placed; the residual OpenCASCADE subtraction-volume anomaly is confined to that auxiliary all-at-once CAD boolean. The actual mesh is generated from 36 independent exact arc-and-line passage volumes, and its volume agrees with the exact clipped-vane calculation to 0.024%, consistent with curved-boundary chord discretization. The final OpenFOAM mesh passes `checkMesh -allGeometry -allTopology`.

Built and verified:
- 320 mm OD, 190 mm ID
- Two 10 mm friction plates in the CAD assembly, with 12 mm between their inner surfaces
- 36 vanes, 8 mm wide, 65 mm radial span, 10° pitch
- 36 disconnected air passages
- 5,616 hexahedra; 156 cells per passage
- Patches: `frictionFace1`, `frictionFace2`, `vanes`, `innerInlet`, `outerOutlet`
- One STL per patch in `constant/triSurface`
- Mesh bounds: ±159.95 mm radially and 0–12 mm axially
- Maximum non-orthogonality 1.691°, maximum skewness 0.0747, maximum aspect ratio 2.169

Chosen assumptions: coarse resolution of 13 radial × 4 circumferential × 3 gapwise cells per passage; 12 arc facets per passage in exported STL; axial origin at the lower friction-face inner surface. The 10 mm plate solids are retained as CAD context but are correctly excluded from the cooling-air mesh. The auxiliary build123d fluid subtraction volume remained unreliable due to an OCC coincident-tool boolean anomaly; passage dimensions, exact analytical volume, Gmsh volume construction, rendered OpenFOAM mesh, and `checkMesh` were checked independently.
